source.title: Fisher-Rao Metric, Geometry, and Complexity of Neural Networks
source.authors: Tengyuan Liang; T. Poggio; A. Rakhlin; James Stokes

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures trained networks' Fisher-Rao norm and generalization gap across network widths and label-randomization levels, using a capacity measure distinct from the claim's original experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper's stated experimental findings about Fisher-Rao norm tracking generalization gap qualify as measured properties of trained networks. Random-label corruption and width are varied, but the text does not report the natural-label and random-label train/test accuracies needed to test V1 directly. The cited Zhang et al. results are prior work, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures Fisher-Rao norms and generalization gaps, but none of the eight versions specifies that relationship. Its width experiment does not establish zero training error or report held-out error separately, so it cannot establish V2's behavior beyond the fitting threshold. Label corruption likewise lacks the separate training and held-out accuracies needed for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experimental conclusion: empirical Fisher-Rao norm appears to track generalization gap across width and label corruption, with a similar qualitative relationship under gradient descent and K-FAC. The authors also establish invariance and norm-comparison properties and generalization bounds; the empirical correlation is evidence for their proposed capacity measure, rather than proof that it controls generalization generally.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies an invariant capacity measure and its relationship to generalization, rather than testing the memorization/generalization coexistence or interventions in the listed claim versions. Its CIFAR-10 experiments vary width and label randomization and compare gradient descent with natural gradient.
record.method_sensitivity: The empirical Fisher-Rao norm and generalization-gap relationship is reported across width and label-randomization levels; the authors say the trend does not appear sensitive to optimizer choice.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical Fisher-Rao norm decreases with width alongside generalization gap for original CIFAR-10 labels. The authors report that the apparent relationship persists across label-corruption levels and under gradient descent and K-FAC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Empirical Fisher-Rao norm appears to track generalization gaps across width and label corruption in fully connected CIFAR-10 networks trained without explicit regularization or augmentation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2019; text also identifies a 2017 preprint)
record.problems: The experimental plots do not provide exact numerical values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The stated generalization-gap relationship is correlational. The paper does not report an explicit capability check for fitting random labels in the described experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results found. Cited results from Zhang et al. and other prior work were excluded because they are not this study's results.

untested.parts: Separate natural-label and random-label training fit and held-out accuracy, including chance-level random-label performance.
Held-out error beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error width threshold after training to convergence.
Image-classification test-error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The piecewise-linear conditioning experiment concerns optimization performance, not V3's image-generalization comparison. Fisher-Rao geometry and the discussion of flatness do not constitute a measurement of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. No additional qualifying result for the listed versions is identifiable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies label randomization but does not report the required natural-label versus random-label training fit and held-out accuracy results.
Width is varied, but the paper does not report test error as a function of width or test the claim that test error keeps falling beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks, or local connectivity, is reported.
The paper compares gradient descent with natural gradient, not adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch generalization-gap experiment is reported.

The paper studies Fisher-Rao norm and its empirical relation to generalization gap, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare the measure with norm- and margin-based measures as V7 specifies.
No memorized-example removal or retraining experiment is reported.

rows.measure: Empirical Fisher-Rao norm and generalization gap
rows.value: The empirical Fisher-Rao norm actually decreases with increasing k, in tandem with the generalization error.
rows.locator: Section 5, Over-parametrization with Hidden Units; Figure 2
rows.note: The paper describes the trend across widths; no exact accuracy or gap values are given in the text.
rows.check: The reported decrease concerns Fisher-Rao norm and generalization gap. Zero training error, convergence, and held-out error separately are not established; this cannot determine V2's post-interpolation effect. The correlation itself is reported, but is outside the listed versions.
